program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s criterion is too permissive: it treats any visible chalk-like texture as complete, and all five traces therefore say yes despite the reference being partial. Refine the typed criteria to distinguish partial stylistic progress from a convincingly completed chalk drawing, using the image as evidence: the edit has grainy, softened drawn treatment, but retains highly photographic detail and recognizable scene elements, so assess whether the overall image—not merely its surface texture—reads as a chalk drawing. Keep partial for meaningful but incomplete transformation, absent for no requested progress, and unknown only when evidence is insufficient. Do not hard-code this example’s label or require unrelated changes; the traces are valid and dependency-free, so this is a criterion/calibration issue, not a transport failure.
